## Competency targets by role level (editorial draft target levels, agent-drafted)

- Issue environmental permits and resource-use authorizations as the deciding authority — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Draft enforceable, implementable binding instruments — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Build and maintain a defensible administrative record — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Negotiate permit conditions, mitigation and agreements using interest-based methods — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Process permit applications and administer issued authorizations — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Operate within, or oversee, delegated and assumed regulatory programs — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
- Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments — journey L2, senior L2, lead L3
- Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Maintain the integrity of regulatory and scientific findings under institutional pressure — journey L2, senior L3, lead L3
- Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty — journey L2, senior L2, lead L2
- Assess litigation exposure and design decisions for resilience on remand — senior L3, lead L3
- Interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Record provenance and AI involvement in work products — journey L1, senior L1, lead L1
- Supervise staff and volunteers in environmental work — senior L3, lead L4
- Design accessible, inclusive public engagement and services — journey L2, senior L3, lead L4
